title: Silas and the Alibi
premise: Ulyana Vane, an insurance investigator with a photographic memory, is hired to close the file on Silas Marchetti, a dockworker's widow who vanished with a half-million-dollar policy unclaimed. But the missing woman's diary keeps being written after her disappearance — entries in handwriting Ulyana recognizes as her own estranged brother's. Following the diary through the harbor district's shuttered cannery, a church soup kitchen, and a forged ledger of payoffs hidden in plain sight among hymn numbers, Ulyana discovers Silas faked her death to escape a smuggling ring that murdered her husband — and that her brother has been sheltering her as his 'alibi' ever since. When the ring closes in and the statute of limitations expires at midnight, Ulyana must choose between closing the case that will make her career and protecting the fragile found family her brother built; she burns the ledger, testifies only against the ringleader, and lets Silas walk free into a new life.
about_author: S. M. Amberdale is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses along the northern coast before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who survive by keeping secrets.

chapters.title: The File That Won't Close
chapters.summary: Ulyana Vane's POV. Ulyana takes the Marchetti case from a rival firm desperate to offload it: a widow vanished fourteen months ago, policy unpaid, statute expiring soon. Her photographic memory catalogs every detail of the thin file. Beat: confident professional boredom masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Diary of a Drowned Woman
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The husband's sister hands over Silas's recovered diary — but the final entry is dated three weeks after the disappearance. Ulyana memorizes it instantly and realizes someone is still writing as Silas. Beat: cold thrill of an impossible detail.

chapters.title: Handwriting I Know
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Comparing the late entries against old family letters, Ulyana identifies the hand: Tomas, her estranged brother, who left home nine years ago after their father's funeral. She hasn't spoken to him since. Beat: betrayal braided with longing.

chapters.title: Harbor Lights
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana travels to Grayhaven Harbor, tracing Silas's last known route past the shuttered Cannery Row and a mission kitchen. The town closes ranks around the missing woman's name. Beat: unease — everyone here knows something.

chapters.title: The Soup Kitchen Nun
chapters.summary: Sister Bernadette's POV. Bernadette feeds drifters and asks no questions, but she remembers a quiet woman who arrived the night Silas 'drowned.' She lies smoothly to the investigator — then prays about lying. Beat: guilt versus mercy.

chapters.title: Tomas
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana confronts Tomas at the boatyard where he repairs engines under a false name. He denies everything with a face she can read like print. Neither mentions the diary. Beat: two people fluent in each other's tells, refusing to speak.

chapters.title: What the Policy Pays For
chapters.summary: Claims manager DeWitt's POV. Back at the office, DeWitt pressures Ulyana: close it as death by misadventure, deny the claim, collect the bonus. He hints the firm's biggest client insured the cannery. Beat: institutional pressure tightening like a vise.

chapters.title: Hymn Numbers
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the mission's donated hymnals, Ulyana notices penciled numbers matching dates and dollar amounts — a ledger disguised as page references. Her memory holds every figure before the book is taken from her. Beat: the case becomes hers, not the firm's.

chapters.title: Silas, Alive
chapters.summary: Silas Marchetti's POV. In a rented room above the bait shop, Silas tends her garden of false identities and reads newspaper coverage of her own drowning. She knows someone is asking questions. Beat: vigilance sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: Nine Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Flashback chapter: the night their father died, what Tomas saw, why he left, and the letter Ulyana never answered. Present-day Ulyana drinks alone and rereads his handwriting. Beat: grief resurfacing, empathy cracking open.

chapters.title: The Cannery Floor
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Breaking into the sealed cannery, Ulyana finds a staging area for cargo that never appears on manifests — and fresh boot prints. Someone uses it still. Beat: dread escalating; she is not alone in the dark.

chapters.title: Men Who Count Crates
chapters.summary: Brannock's POV. Introduce Brannock, the harbor fixer who runs the smuggling line and once employed Silas's husband. He learns an insurance investigator is sniffing around. Beat: predator calmly noting prey.

chapters.title: An Alibi Made of Love
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas explains nothing to Ulyana but we learn everything: he found Silas half-drowned, hid her, and began writing her diary to establish she was alive elsewhere — an alibi built from fiction. Beat: tenderness inside deception.

chapters.title: Photographic
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana reconstructs the entire ledger from memory in a motel room, mapping payments to cannery shipments and one recurring recipient: a shell company tied to her own firm's client. Beat: vertigo of complicity — her employer is inside the machine.

chapters.title: DeWitt's Warning
chapters.summary: DeWitt's POV. DeWitt calls Ulyana off, offering promotion and a quiet threat. Ulyana hears in his phrasing exactly which words he was told to use. Beat: the professional mask slipping into menace.

chapters.title: The Widow Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas ventures out to warn Tomas and glimpses Ulyana across the market — and recognizes the investigator's face from a photograph in Tomas's wallet. Beat: fear that love has left a trail.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Legal countdown established: twelve days until the claim lapses forever, freeing the money and freezing the truth. Ulyana calculates what closing honestly would cost Tomas. Beat: clock now audible in every scene.

chapters.title: Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Tomas and Ulyana POV alternating. On the mudflats, Tomas finally admits Silas lives; Ulyana admits she's known for days. Siblings argue over whether truth or protection matters more. Beat: rupture — the case and the family are now the same wound.

chapters.title: The Husband's Grave
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the cemetery Ulyana finds evidence Silas's husband's 'accident' was staged: the same hymn-number code carved into a maintenance log. He discovered the ledger first. Beat: sorrow hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Bernadette Breaks
chapters.summary: Sister Bernadette's POV. Brannock leans on the mission; Bernadette must choose between her vows of discretion and a girl hiding upstairs. She moves Silas through the confessional corridor. Beat: faith tested and quietly kept.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana realizes she's being followed through Grayhaven's fog and uses her memory of the town map to lose the tail in the fish market. Beat: cat-and-mouse energy; competence as survival.

chapters.title: What Brannock Keeps in the Safe
chapters.summary: Brannock's POV. Inside Brannock's safe: the original ledger page, photos of Silas alive, and a file on Tomas. He now has leverage on everyone. Beat: the trap assembling itself.

chapters.title: The Bait Shop Burn
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Arson destroys the room above the bait shop and Silas's cache of identities. She escapes with nothing but the diary's true final pages. Beat: loss stripping her to essentials.

chapters.title: Brother Against File
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana offers Tomas a deal: turn state's evidence, testify against Brannock, lose Silas's anonymity. He refuses — he'd rather be guilty than grateful. Beat: the siblings' central conflict at full heat.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger Aloud
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana decodes the full scheme: the client firm laundered smuggling profits through fake claims, including Silas's husband's death payout. The diary entries were timestamps. Beat: revelation clicking into place like tumblers.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Mission
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Brannock's men raid the mission; Bernadette rings the bell; Tomas takes a beating buying time; Silas slips out the coal chute. Beat: chaos, sacrifice, near-catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Photograph
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Brannock shows Ulyana a photo of her and Tomas together — proof of collusion — and offers the file back if she surrenders the decoded ledger. Beat: temptation priced in blood.

chapters.title: Everything I Remember
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Alone, Ulyana recites from memory every entry, figure, and face of the whole case, deciding what memory is for: winning, or witnessing. Beat: quiet turning point; she chooses witness.

chapters.title: Silas Decides
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas chooses to stop running: she'll surface publicly just long enough to sign away the policy and bury Brannock's claim on her silence. Beat: agency reclaimed; the hunted becomes the witness.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana drafts a report naming her own firm while DeWitt circulates a termination order. She mails copies to the insurance commission and a journalist. Beat: point of no return, professionally and personally.

chapters.title: The Cannery Reunion
chapters.summary: Ulyana, Tomas, Silas POV braided. The three meet secretly in the cannery where it all began, trading what they know and planning the endgame before midnight of the statute date. Beat: wary alliance becoming found family.

chapters.title: Brannock Closes In
chapters.summary: Brannock's POV. Brannock learns of the meeting, sets fire to the cannery's remaining wing, and calls DeWitt to make sure no claim will ever honor what happens next. Beat: villainy at its most efficient.

chapters.title: Fire on Cannery Row
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Trapped by smoke, Ulyana navigates the burning building from memory, pulling Silas out through the loading tunnel as the ledger's physical copies burn. Beat: climax ignites; memory outlasts paper.

chapters.title: Midnight, Statute Expired
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At 12:01 a.m., the claim legally dies — and with it Brannock's leverage, since there is no longer any money to extort or deny. Ulyana files her true report anyway. Beat: exhale after the held breath.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas testifies under her real name about her husband's murder and the smuggling line; Brannock is indicted; DeWitt resigns rather than face the commission. Beat: justice arriving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: What Tomas Chose
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas accepts a plea for obstruction, choosing months of honest consequence over another decade of fiction. Ulyana waits outside the courthouse. Beat: accountability as an act of love.

chapters.title: The Claim Nobody Paid
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Epilogue-of-sorts: the policy is voided, the bonus lost, Ulyana unemployed — and strangely light. She visits the grave of Silas's husband and leaves the restored diary. Beat: cost tallied, worth weighed.

chapters.title: Grayhaven in Spring
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Months later: Bernadette's mission reopens its kitchen, Tomas works his last weeks before sentencing, Silas plants a real garden. Ulyana returns without a case attached. Beat: belonging taking root.

chapters.title: A New Entry
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas begins writing a diary again — this time as herself, first entry dated today. She writes down the names of everyone who kept her. Beat: healing rendered as handwriting.

chapters.title: Silas and the Alibi
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana and Tomas walk the seawall; he asks why she burned her career for strangers. She answers that they weren't strangers — they were the family that formed while she wasn't looking. Final image: the tide erasing footprints, none needed as proof. Beat: resolution, warmth, and earned peace.
